title: To a Place of No Return

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The goat will carry on itself all their sins to a remote place; and the man shall release it in the wilderness." - Lev 16:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A remote place. Somewhere far off, uninhabited, where nothing lives and no one goes. The goat is released, and it does not come back.

Israel watched it go. The animal grew smaller against the horizon until they could not see it any more — and with it went everything Aaron had confessed.

Some of us need to watch that goat.

We carry sins that God dealt with years ago. We wake at three in the morning and the memory arrives again, and we relive it, and we apologise to God for it once more. The thing we did to someone. The years we wasted. The failure we cannot forgive ourselves for.

But hear this carefully: God is not asking you to forgive yourself. He is asking you to believe Him. Your sin is not gone because you have finally made peace with it. It is gone because Christ carried it away.

I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions, for my own sake, and remembers your sins no more (Isa 43:25). Remembers them no more. God is not still thinking about it.

The accuser will keep bringing it back. That is his job (Rev 12:10). Do not accept delivery of what God has sent away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What sin do you keep retrieving that God has removed?
2. Are you trying to "forgive yourself" rather than believing God's word?
3. How would your prayer life change if you truly believed it was gone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You remember my sins no more. When the accusations come back, help me to believe Your word over my feelings and to rest in what Christ has carried away. Amen.
